what_it_does: Introduces a new sparsity pattern for neural network accelerators that improves both training accuracy and hardware efficiency. Traditional one-dimensional sparsity patterns (where certain weights are zeroed out) lose too much accuracy in large language models, but this work identifies a two-dimensional block-based sparsity pattern that works better by exploiting the mathematical relationship between forward and backward passes in training. The hardware accelerator dynamically switches between row-wise and column-wise storage formats to handle this sparsity pattern efficiently, achieving significant improvements in memory bandwidth and computational throughput.
